title: Model binding policy: deterministic selection across tag, semver ranges, and commit hashes
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers need a single, predictable contract for how the Redwood API/SDK resolves a user-supplied model identifier when multiple selector types are supported (human tag, semver ranges, and repository commit hash). Existing behaviour is sometimes ambiguous across SDKs and runtimes which has caused unexpected upgrades or fallbacks in customer production traffic.

Goal: Define a deterministic, auditable resolution algorithm and SDK surface that ensures: 1) explicit identifiers (commit hash) are stable and highest-priority; 2) semver-range selectors behave predictably with clear rules for pre-release vs stable windows; 3) tag-based selectors (user-friendly names) are supported but treated as lower precedence and instrumented extensively for visibility. The contract should be simple to implement in the runtime and SDKs, allow safe automatic fallbacks, and provide clear error semantics when resolution is ambiguous or disallowed by policy (e.g., pinned by org policy).

Scope: API changes (server-side resolution and new error codes), SDK-expanded pin selector types and resolver helpers, runtime acceptance of multiple selector fields, telemetry schema for resolution decisions, migration notes for customers using tag-only pins. Excludes change to model publishing workflows or storage format for artifacts.

Non-goals: Changing how models are served after resolution (that is separate rollout/traffic routing work), introducing new pin syntaxes beyond tag/semver/hash, or altering access control behavior (RBAC remains unchanged).
acceptance_criteria: Server resolves 'model_request' with up to three selector fields (tag, semver_range, commit_hash) according to the precedence rules and returns the final model ref and resolution path in response metadata.
SDK helper APIs provide a small surface: ModelSelector(tag?: string, semver?: string, hash?: string) and a local validator that reproduces server precedence for pre-submission checks.
If resolution results in a downgrade or upgrade outside an allowed window, server returns 409 with structured resolution_details explaining candidate versions and reasons.
Telemetry events capture chosen selector, fallback steps, prior candidate set, and latency of resolution; events documented in console and exposed in per-route traces.
Compatibility test matrix covering: tag-only, semver-only, hash-only, tag+semver, semver+hash, and all three combined with mock registry demonstrating bucketing across precedence permutations.
Migration doc (console + API docs) published that outlines recommended practices and examples for migrating tag-only pins to semver or hash pins.
Edge-case behavior defined for pre-release semver ranges (e.g., ^1.2.0 includes 1.2.3-beta? -> No unless range explicitly allows pre-release) and communicated in API spec.
E2E integration test that verifies SDK-local validation matches server resolution for 95% of random selector inputs and logs divergence cases for manual triage.
Backwards-compatible default: if client provides only tag (existing behavior), resolution preserves current runtime semantics but adds a warning in response metadata encouraging stronger pins.
Documentation includes canonical examples and recommended patterns for production (hash for strict reproducibility, semver for safe upgrades, tag for convenience).
implementation_steps: Design: finalize precedence order, semver pre-release rules, and error codes (ENG/PM review).
API: add resolution_metadata to generation responses and new 409/422 structured errors for resolution conflicts. Update OpenAPI spec.
Runtime: implement deterministic resolver that accepts three optional selector inputs and applies precedence rules. Ensure resolver is idempotent and logs resolution path to tracing span.
SDKs: implement ModelSelector helper, local validator, and a small opt-in warning layer that surfaces server warnings preflight. Add unit tests reproducing server resolver behaviour.
Tests: create a registry fixture with synthetic versions and tags; write unit, integration, and e2e tests covering permutations.
Telemetry: add resolution.choice, resolution.fallback_count, resolution.candidate_list fields to events; wire to console model-onboarding dashboard.
Docs: publish API migration guide, SDK usage examples, and in-console migration checklist for customers.
Rollout: behind feature flag for 2 weeks in staging, then gated rollout to 10% of hosted traffic for validation before full rollout.

notes: Precedence (proposed): 1) commit_hash (exact) -> 2) semver range (highest satisfying release, prefer stable over pre-release unless range allows) -> 3) tag (named alias).

Fallback rules: if commit_hash not found -> return 404 resolution error unless 'allow_fallback' flag is set, then evaluate semver/he tag; if semver resolves to a version with breaking ABI mismatch, return 409 with details.

SDK ergonomics: keep surface minimal to avoid combinatorial explosion; expose ModelSelector factory and a toString() for logging. Provide a strict mode that refuses sending requests that would result in ambiguous resolution.
Telemetry: resolution.choice values: ['hash','semver','tag','none'] and resolution.reason e.g. 'exact-match','semver-stable','tag-alias','fallback-enabled','policy-blocked'.

Migration suggestion: customers running tag-only pins for critical traffic should migrate to hash pins for reproducibility; semver pins recommended for libraries and shared endpoints where controlled upgrades are desired.
